'''''Riccia cavernosa''','' also known as '''cavernous crystalwort''',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Riccia cavernosa |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/learning/species-finder/riccia-cavernosa/ |website=britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk}}</ref> is a species of [[liverwort]] which belongs to the family [[Ricciaceae]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Riccia cavernosa Hoffm. |url=https://www.gbif.org/species/5710073 |access-date=2026-01-06 |website=www.gbif.org |language=en}}</ref> 

== Description ==
[[File:Riccia cavernosa 167051725.jpg|thumb|Close up of its leaf.]]
''R. cavernosa'' develops in rounded rosettes that can reach up to 3 cm in diameter, consisting of numerous lobes that are either oblong or rounded, with their widest part located above the midpoint. The lobes can measure up to 2.5 mm in width and feature a tip that is more or less truncate. Typically, the plants exhibit a yellow-green colour, lacking any reddish pigmentation, and they maintain a yellowish appearance even when dried. The upper surface displays a very short, subtle groove located solely at the tip, along with perforations that extend nearly to the tips of the branches.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Riccia cavernosa {{!}} Cavernous Crystalwort |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Riccia-cavernosa.pdf |website=britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Cavernous Crystalwort {{!}} NatureSpot |url=https://www.naturespot.org/species/cavernous-crystalwort |access-date=2026-01-06 |website=www.naturespot.org}}</ref>

== Discovery ==
At present, it is estimated that there are 250 species of ''Riccia'', with 152 being widely recognized, while the rest are classified as either 'doubtful' or 'poorly known'.<ref name=":0" />

''Riccia cavernosa'' was identified in [[New Zealand]] in February 2016, found at the edges of several artificial wetlands created to support the recovery of a threatened native wading bird == Habitat ==
''R. cavernosa'' is generally found in moist, exposed environments with neutral to base-rich mud found near reservoirs, lakes, and ponds. It can also be found in damp depressions within agricultural fields, gravel pits, and sand dunes.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Riccia cavernosa Cavernous Crystalwort {{!}} West Glamorgan Flora |url=http://www.westglamorganflora.org.uk/bryophytes/riccia-cavernosa/34525/ |access-date=2026-01-06 |website=www.westglamorganflora.org.uk}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 2022, ''R. cavernosa'' was awarded the [[Moss of the Year in Latvia|Latvian moss of the year]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Make way for the Moss of the Year 2022 |url=https://eng.lsm.lv/article/society/environment/make-way-for-the-moss-of-the-year-2022.a439249/ |access-date=2026-01-06 |website=eng.lsm.lv |language=en}}</ref>
